answer: Lantern Quorum Handshake. Each agent identity must publish a distinct random cipher seed and solve a fresh challenge derived from it before any peer accepts its messages. Honest agents derive seeds once from local entropy and reuse them cheaply. A sybil operator must independently generate and solve a new seed-challenge pair per fake identity, paying full compute and latency each time, and duplicated seeds collide and get flagged. A shared nebula overlay then cross-checks seed uniqueness across peers, so clones surface as visible conflicts rather than hiding.
